issues.description: The problem text explicitly requires the Animal.name attribute to use StringBuilder for efficient modifications, but the solution implementation defines the attribute as a String. This mismatch (StringBuilder vs String) can confuse students about the expected attribute type and will cause discrepancies when they follow the textual instruction. It may also lead to failing structural checks if tests expect a StringBuilder field or getter/setter signatures using StringBuilder.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the specification: change the Animal.name attribute to a StringBuilder. Update the constructor to initialize the StringBuilder (e.g., this.name = new StringBuilder(name)), and adapt the getter and setter to use StringBuilder (or have the getter return StringBuilder and the setter accept String or StringBuilder). Update all usages in subclasses (concatenation will call toString() on StringBuilder) accordingly.

issues.description: Within the problem statement there is an internal contradiction: the UML shows the Animal.name attribute as type String, while the textual instruction (later) requires using StringBuilder for the name attribute. This inconsistency can confuse students about which type they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem specification consistent by updating the UML to show name: StringBuilder (or remove the textual instruction and keep name: String). Preferably update the UML to match the textual requirement to use StringBuilder so all parts of the specification agree.
